Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

watch out! interjection

also look out, careful!, mind!, beware, beware of the dog

classical

Petr. 29.1: CAVĒ CANEM
Plaut. Most. 324b: Cavē nē cadās, astā.

Cavē!

imperative of <span lang="la">caveō</span>: alone; with an accusative (<span lang="la">cavē canem</span>); with <span lang="la">nē</span> and the subjunctive, or the bare subjunctive (<span lang="la">cavē cadās</span>); plural <span lang="la">cavēte</span>

watch out! mind!

In comedy often with sīs (“mind, will you”). In Plautus’ verse the final vowel is often shortened in speech (cave); the word is cavē.

Other words

  • Cavē tibi! — look out for yourself! mind out!

    also used · classical · Plaut. Aul. 584: cavē sīs tibi; Plaut. Bacch. 1033

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

  • Cavētō! — beware! (a warning that stands)

    future imperative of <span lang="la">caveō</span> · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.4.85: hic niger est, hunc tū, Rōmāne, cavētō

    The future imperative of rules and warnings that hold from now on.

Examples

  • canis ingēns, catēnā vīnctus, in pariete erat pictus superque quadrātā litterā scrīptum CAVĒ CANEM

    a huge dog on a chain was painted on the wall, and above it in capitals BEWARE OF THE DOGPetr. 29.1

  • Cavē nē cadās, astā.

    Careful you don’t fall; stand still.Plaut. Most. 324b

  • Cavē sīs malam rem.

    Mind you don’t get into trouble.Plaut. Asin. 43

  • hic niger est, hunc tū, Rōmāne, cavētō

    he is a black heart: Roman, beware of himHor. S. 1.4.85

See also careful, don’t fall, mind your fingers, take care, stop right there!.
